items.title: Four workers hit by train in Japan
items.summary: TOKYO: Four people were unconscious in Japan on Thursday after being hit by a train, authorities said, with one media report saying they were "without vital signs." The incident involving four workers took place at Shin-Kanuma Station north of Tokyo, the fire department said. "When emergency services arrived, three workers were still trapped under the train, while one was on the platform," a fire department spokesman told AFP.

items.title: Johor police arrest five, open three investigation papers over upside-down flags
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 20 – Police have arrested five individuals, while three investigation papers opened following several recent cases involving the Malaysian flag and the Johor state flag being displayed upside-down in the state. Johor deputy police chief Hoo Chuan Huat said the arrests were from three reported cases that were under the Kulai, Iskandar Puteri and Johor Bahru South police jurisdictions. “So far, police have opened three investigation papers involving the three cases.

items.title: Immigration lorry driver charged with causing death of three family members in crash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: An Immigration Department lorry driver today claimed trial at the magistrates' court here to five charges, including three counts of causing death by reckless or dangerous driving in connection with yesterday's fatal crash at the Maju Junction intersection. He was charged under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 with causing the deaths of Shaik Mohd Firdaus Shaik Yahya, 53, and his two daughters, Siti Norshazlin, 25, and Siti Darwisyah Auni, 12. The three family members died after the lorry allegedly crashed into a Proton Saga before losing control and hitting four pedestrians at the Jalan Sultan Ismail intersection at 1am yesterday.

items.title: Saarani: Ex-aide quit over health reasons, no speculation over drug claims
items.summary: IPOH: Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad today said no assumptions should be made over social media claims that his former political secretary, Mohamad Hamidi Baharuddin, was involved in drugs. Saarani said Mohamad Hamidi had resigned from the post, effective Aug 17, citing health reasons. Asked about Mohamad Hamidi's replacement, Saarani said the appointment would be made in due course.

items.title: Khalid rejects 'dead horse' jibe over Tabung Haji RCI
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Amanah has dismissed a political leader's claim that the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Lembaga Tabung Haji was merely "flogging a dead horse", saying the issues raised remain relevant and require action. Amanah communications director Khalid Abdul Samad said the RCI should not be dismissed as a futile exercise as it had highlighted alleged irregularities, corruption and abuse of power. "A political party leader recently said the RCI is flogging a dead horse.

items.title: KL-Karak widening project to be completed one year ahead of schedule
items.summary: GOMBAK: The RM2.1 billion Kuala Lumpur-Karak Highway widening project is expected to be completed in 2029, a year ahead of schedule, Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said. The project, fully funded by AFA Prime, involves widening 45.3 kilometres of the KL-Karak between Gombak and Bentong, as well as constructing a 999-metre third tunnel at Genting Sempah. Nanta said the government is also taking broader measures to improve road safety and reduce traffic accidents and fatalities nationwide.

items.title: Govt approves 17 measures to tighten security at KLIA, international entry points
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 20 — The Cabinet has approved 17 recommendations to strengthen security controls, screening and risk management at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) and the country’s international entry points. The government will also strengthen e-vetting and access controls for flight crew, airline employees, airport operations and ground-handling personnel, airport operator staff, vendors, contractors and others requiring access to restricted security areas. The ministries said the six measures form the short-term priorities under a broader plan to strengthen the integrity of security controls at KLIA and the country’s international entry points.

items.title: Telcos must explain excessive prepaid line registrations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil will ask telecommunications companies (telcos) to explain allegations that excessive numbers of prepaid lines are being registered under individuals' names and potentially misused for scams. Fahmi said he took note of concerns raised by Muslim Consumers Association of Malaysia (PPIM) chief activist Datuk Nadzim Johan, including claims that people had discovered numerous phone lines registered under their names without their knowledge. Fahmi said the government had already introduced several safeguards, including requiring prepaid line registrations to be verified using MyDigital ID.

items.title: Kedah police open 69 disciplinary probes involving 90 personnel this year
items.summary: ALOR STAR: Kedah police have opened 69 disciplinary investigation papers involving 90 policemen, personnel and civilian staff this year for alleged misconduct, including criminal offences, corruption, drug-related offences, traffic violations and Syariah offences. He said the 2025 cases involved 39 senior police officers, 248 junior policemen and seven civilian personnel. "Of the cases opened, 33 involved criminal offences, four commercial offences, three Syariah offences, seven corruption cases and 24 drug-related offences," he said.

items.title: Malaysia Airlines flight bound for KL aborts takeoff at Japan’s Narita airport
items.summary: CHIBA, Aug 20 — A Malaysian Airlines plane bound for Kuala Lumpur aborted takeoff Thursday morning at Narita airport near Tokyo due to a problem with the aircraft, Kyodo News reported the transport ministry said. Black smoke was reportedly seen coming from the airplane when it was moving onto one of the airport's runways at around 10.40am local time. Separately, Xinhua, citing public broadcaster NHK reported Narita Airport said the incident prompted the closure of Runway A, which is currently being inspected.

items.title: Meta trial rocked by claim safety tools were 'designed to fail'
items.summary: OAKLAND: A former employee testified on Wednesday that some of Meta's safety tools for Facebook and Instagram were "designed to fail," contradicting the company's defence strategy in a landmark trial in California. For a second day, Meta is fending off accusations by a coalition of US states that it deliberately designed its products to hook children and gather their data while misleading the public. However, Meta made some of those tools opt-in, meaning that users had to intentionally turn them on, including a feature launched in 2021 called "Take a Break," which lets users set reminders to take breaks from scrolling on Instagram.

items.title: RM7.93m drug haul: Nine nabbed after police bust raft house stash
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: A floating raft house in Masai was allegedly used by a drug syndicate as a storage hub before police busted the operation, arresting nine suspects and seizing drugs worth RM7.93 million. The syndicate, believed to have been operating since January, allegedly used the raft house to store drugs, while another house was used to process ecstasy pills. "Two machines used to process ecstasy pills and equipment for repackaging the drugs were also seized.

items.title: Immigration lorry driver arrives in court over fatal Jalan Sultan Ismail crash [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Immigration Department lorry driver involved in the fatal crash along Jalan Sultan Ismail yesterday arrived at the magistrates' court here today under heavy police escort. The 43-year-old suspect arrived at 12pm, escorted by several police officers into the courtroom. The suspect was detained to assist investigations following the crash at the Jalan Sultan Ismail intersection early Wednesday morning.

items.title: Zambry: Independent committee to draft new law after Auku repeal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: An independent committee will be established to engage stakeholders and determine the framework for a new legislation to replace the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (Auku) following its repeal. Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said the repeal would require several immediate measures, including a transitional legal mechanism to prevent a regulatory void as Auku currently serves as the principal law governing public universities. Zambry said repealing Auku was in line with the ministry's long-term plan to introduce a single, comprehensive "One Higher Education Act", as outlined in the Malaysia Higher Education Plan 2026-2035.

items.title: 'Breakthrough' mRNA cancer drug cuts melanoma recurrence in major trial
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US drugmakers Merck and Moderna said Wednesday a personalised cancer treatment had shown success in reducing the recurrence of melanoma tumors in a late-stage trial hailed by experts as a "breakthrough." The drug, called "intismeran autogene," is based on the same messenger RNA (mRNA) technology behind Covid-19 vaccines. "Today marks an extraordinary milestone for Moderna, for mRNA science and, most importantly, for patients with cancer," Moderna CEO Stephane Bancel said in a statement.

items.title: Factory supervisor arrested over upside-down Jalur Gemilang, Johor flag
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI: Police arrested a factory supervisor yesterday after the Jalur Gemilang and Johor flag were found flying upside down at a factory in Gelang Patah here. He said police received a report the next day and inspected the premises. "Checks found 3 flagpoles in front of the premises, with one Jalur Gemilang and one Johor flag flown upside down.

items.title: Balancing independence, cooperation in middle power politics
items.summary: LETTERS: On July 21, eight Democratic members of the US Congress wrote to Secretary of State Marco Rubio urging the suspension of International Military Education and Training funding to Malaysia unless Putrajaya reversed Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's directive to deport Israeli nationals holding dual citizenship. Three weeks later, on Aug 13, a White House report on transhipment placed Malaysia in its second tier of economies accused of laundering Chinese exports to evade US tariffs. Sixty-nine years later, the durability of the relationship does not depend on Malaysia choosing the United States over China.

items.title: Malaysia's trade hits record RM364.7bil in July as exports soar 38pct, surplus stretches 75 months
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's trade hit a record monthly high in July, rising 37.3 per cent year-on-year (YoY) to RM364.74 billion, driven by strong growth in both exports and imports. The Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry said exports increased 38 per cent YoY to a record RM193.60 billion, while imports grew 36.4 per cent to RM171.14 billion. This resulted in a trade surplus of RM22.46 billion, extending Malaysia's surplus streak to 75 consecutive months since May 2020.

items.title: Ranhill's valuation running ahead of fundamentals – Analysts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The valuation of Ranhill Utilities Bhd is running ahead of its fundamentals, said BIMB Securities, as it expects the Johor water utilities operator's core earnings to decline 27.6 per cent year-on-year in the financial year ending June 30, 2027 (FY27F). "While we remain positive on Ranhill's longer-term exposure to Johor's rising water demand and infrastructure expansion, we believe the recent share price re-rating has increasingly priced in these structural catalysts ahead of their earnings contribution," said BIMB Securities. Ranhill SAJ Sdn Bhd, the water operator of Johor, is 80 per cent owned by Ranhill.

items.title: Ecuador intel chief, five Americans killed in Kenya helicopter crash
items.summary: NAIROBI: Ecuador's intelligence chief and five US citizens died when a tourist helicopter crashed in central Kenya on Wednesday, killing all seven people on board, officials said. The accident happened Wednesday morning in Samburu County, north of the capital Nairobi, according to the Kenya Civil Aviation Authority (KCAA). It said difficult terrain hampered rescue operations.

items.title: Son honours father who worked 25 years as a cleaner to support family
items.summary: KAJANG: "Since I was young, I have never been ashamed of my father's job as a cleaner. In fact, I am proud because it is noble work," said 25-year-old Mohamad Zulfithri Mohd Johari. "My father has worked at the R&R for 25 years and still earns a living there today.

items.title: Johor factory ordered shut after Jalur Gemilang, state flag flown upside down
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Aug 20 — The Iskandar Puteri City Council (MBIP) has ordered a factory located at the Southern Industrial and Logistics Clusters (SiLC) Industrial Park here to cease operations after it was found to have displayed a Jalur Gemilang and the Johor state flag upside down. The city council said the industrial factory was also issued a compound for displaying an unlicensed billboard and did not have a valid license to operate a business. MBIP said further inspection found that the premises did not have a business license and the premises owner was issued a notice for operating a business without a valid license.

items.title: NASA satellite rescue mission fails
items.summary: WASHINGTON: A complicated mission to save a NASA satellite from burning up in the atmosphere has failed, the US space agency said Wednesday, as the rescue spacecraft could not be controlled. The unprecedented US$30 million dollar mission attempted to send a robot to grab the telescope and move it farther into orbit. Planners had hoped the mission would pave the way for giving other satellites a second life.

items.title: New RM20mil motorsport circuit in Perlis to boost border tourism
items.summary: PADANG BESAR: The RM20 million motorsport circuit under construction at the Chuping Valley Industrial Area (CVIA) is expected to boost Perlis' economy and border tourism by attracting motorsport enthusiasts from Malaysia and Thailand. Menteri Besar Abu Bakar Hamzah said the 1.3km circuit would serve as a new tourism attraction while supporting local businesses and the wider state economy. Abu Bakar said the circuit was expected to draw more Thai visitors, particularly motorsport enthusiasts, who could also spend on accommodation, food and other goods and services in Perlis.

items.title: BMI raises 2026 average CPO price forecast to RM4,453 on tight supply
items.summary: In its latest Palm Oil Price Forecast report, BMI said this represents a year-on-year (y-o-y) 4.1 per cent rise from the 2025 average of RM4,279 per tonne. As of the Aug 17 market close, front-month Bursa Malaysia-listed palm oil settled at RM4,589 per tonne, a year-to-date gain of 16.1 per cent and a year-to-date average of RM4,380 per tonne, said BMI. BMI also said it has revised down Malaysia's palm oil production forecast and expects output to ease 3.5 per cent y-o-y to 19.5 million tonnes in the 2026/2027 season.

items.title: Five held over upside-down Jalur Gemilang, Johor flags in state
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Five people have been arrested as police investigate three separate cases involving the Jalur Gemilang and Johor state flags flown upside down across the state. Johor deputy police chief Deputy Commissioner Hoo Chuan Huat said investigation papers had been opened in Kulai, Iskandar Puteri and Johor Baru South. In Iskandar Puteri, police detained a 56-year-old man.

items.title: Australia jobless rate hits near 5-year high of 4.5pct in July
items.summary: SYDNEY: Australian employment unexpectedly fell in July and the jobless rate hit its highest point since late 2021, data showed on Thursday, adding to signs of a cooling labour market and easing pressure for another interest rate hike. The report sent the Australian dollar down 0.2 per cent to US$0.7111. The participation rate eased to 66.9 per cent from 67 per cent, hours worked dropped 0.6 per cent and the underemployment rate - a measure of slack in the labour market - held at a two-year high of 6.4 per cent.

items.title: CK Hutchison seeks over US$1.5 billion from Panama over port takeover
items.summary: HONG KONG: Hong Kong conglomerate CK Hutchison said on Thursday it has filed international arbitration proceedings against Panama over its cancellation of a concession to operate two ports in the Panama Canal. The dispute stems from a Panama supreme court ruling in January that struck down the contract that let Panama Ports Company (PPC), a unit of CK Hutchison, manage the canal's Pacific port of Balboa and the Atlantic port at Cristobal. "The Company is seeking damages of more than US$1.5 billion for the destruction of the Company's investments in Panama," the firm's board of directors said in a filing to the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.

items.title: UK threatens sanctions as Israel advances West Bank settlement plan
items.summary: LONDON: Britain said on Wednesday it had summoned Israel's charge d'affaires and demanded a halt to a major West Bank settlement project after Israeli authorities opened bidding for more than 1,200 homes in the area. The project would further separate east Jerusalem, occupied and annexed by Israel and predominantly inhabited by Palestinians, from the West Bank. "The Israeli Government must halt E1 plans immediately, retract the tender and stop all settlement expansion," Miliband said in a statement.

items.title: Cabinet approves 17 measures, six quick wins to tighten KLIA, border security
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Cabinet has approved 17 recommendations to strengthen security controls, screening and risk management at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) and the country's international entry points. The recommendations, contained in a joint memorandum by the Home Ministry and Transport Ministry, were approved yesterday. The ministry said security and intelligence information-sharing through the National Immigration Command Centre (NICC) would also be strengthened.

items.title: Lim Lip Eng accuses police of double standards over flag incidents
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Kepong member of parliament Lim Lip Eng has accused police of applying double standards in their handling of two flag-related incidents involving a factory in Johor and the Kuala Terengganu City Council. Lim said a Nepali security guard and a local woman in Kulai were detained and remanded for four days after the Jalur Gemilang and Johor flags were displayed upside down. he said.

items.title: 'More confrontational': Iran's new hardline security leadership
items.summary: Khamenei, in power since his father Ali Khamenei was killed at the start of the US-Israeli war against Iran in February, has yet to be seen in public since taking on the top job and his health and influence remain uncertain. But on August 9 and 10 he filled key security posts – many of which became vacant after previous incumbents were killed in the war – with loyal, veteran figures hailing from the Revolutionary Guards (IRGC), Iran's ideological army, which has a long history of antagonism with the US. They included Mohsen Rezaei, 71, a former commander of the IRGC for almost all the 1980s war against Saddam Hussein's Iraq and Hossein Taeb, 63, a former Guards intelligence chief who stepped down in mysterious circumstances in 2022.

items.title: Housewife loses nearly RM40,000 in online job scam
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU: A housewife lost nearly RM40,000 after falling victim to an online job scam promising lucrative commissions. District police chief Assistant Commissioner Azli Mohd Noor said the 36-year-old victim lodged a police report on Aug 19 after realising she had been duped. He said the victim made five transactions to several different bank accounts totalling RM38,505 between Aug 15 and Aug 18.

items.title: Asian stocks rally as US Treasury steps in to ease bond fears
items.summary: HONG KONG: Asian markets rallied Thursday after the US Treasury said it would "at least double" the amount of long-term bonds to push down borrowing costs, after they surged this week to near two-decade highs. The surprise move provided a much-needed shot in the arm for investors worried about a spike in 10- and 30-year yields caused by the prospect of inflation staying elevated, government borrowing and possible Federal Reserve interest rate hikes. Soon after the announcement, US equities reversed losses to end higher while the dollar tumbled against its peers as traders breathed a sigh of relief following a fresh bout of selling.

items.title: Thunderstorm warning in effect for Sarawak, Sabah, and Labuan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 20 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in several areas in Sarawak, Sabah and Labuan until 11 am this morning. According to the warning issued at 8.50 am, the areas expected to be affected in Sarawak include Betong (Saratok), Sarikei, Mukah (Daro, Matu, Mukah and Dalat), Miri (Beluru and Marudi), Limbang, Kapit (Belaga) and Bintulu (Tatau). In addition, the same weather warning has also been issued for the entire Federal Territory of Labuan.

items.title: Rocky case: Owner also hit with animal cruelty charge over dog’s death
items.summary: KLANG, Aug 20 — The owner of the dog named Rocky has also been charged in the Sessions Court here with cruelty against the animal that died following an incident involving council dogcatchers. S Roghini Devi pleaded not guilty after the charge was read before Judge Mujib Saroji. DVS prosecuting officer Sharif Sabran appeared for the prosecution, while lawyers Choo Dee Wei and Jeremy Vignesh represented Roghini.

items.title: Rocky case: Klang council volunteer claims trial over alleged animal cruelty in dog’s death
items.summary: KLANG, Aug 20 — A volunteer with the Klang city council claimed trial in the Sessions Court today for allegedly committing animal cruelty against a dog named Rocky during a stray dog-catching operation last month. Shah Idham Nor Haikal Shaharom is accused of causing unnecessary pain or suffering to the animal by strangling it with a looped rope outside a residence in Taman Teluk Gedong Indah, Port Klang, on July 29, FMT reported. The incident occurred during an enforcement operation in Port Klang on July 29, which resulted in Rocky's death.

items.title: Six including two children survive falling tree crash in Melaka
items.summary: JASIN, Aug 20 — Six individuals including two children had a narrow escape when the vehicle they were travelling in was hit by a fallen tree at KM 24, Kampung Air Panas, Bemban here last night. Melaka Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) public relations officer Deputy Fire Superintendent II Mohd Hafidzatullah Rashid said his department received an emergency call at 9.46 pm and a team of personnel from Jasin Bestari Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) was dispatched to the location. He said the Jasin Bestari BBP fire brigade team, with the assistance of Jasin BBP, carried out the work of cutting and clearing the tree and the operation was completed at 11.01 pm.

items.title: Six Sarawak areas hit ‘Unhealthy’ air levels as API readings spike
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 20 — Six areas in Sarawak recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at an unhealthy level as of 9 am today. Meanwhile, 50 other areas nationwide recorded API readings at a moderate level (51-100), while another 12 areas still maintained good air quality (below 50). API data is released hourly based on readings from 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide.

items.title: NRD quashes claims of Rohingya getting MyKad, says non-citizens also have legal matters at its premises
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 20 — The National Registration Department (NRD) has moved to quell social media speculation after a viral video showing alleged Rohingya at its premises was linked to unfounded claims regarding the issuance of MyKad to non-citizens. In June, NRD addressed a similar issue where a viral clip caused widespread confusion between the registration of a non-citizen’s birth and the granting of Malaysian citizenship. ‘Pink’ birth certificate explained To prevent further misunderstanding, NRD reiterated that a pink birth certificate serves only as proof that a birth occurred and was registered within Malaysia.

items.title: Police examine CCTV, dashcam footage to reconstruct deadly Immigration lorry crash on Jalan Sultan Ismail
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 20 — Police are reviewing dashcam and closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage to reconstruct a fatal accident involving an Immigration Department lorry that killed a father and his two daughters in Jalan Sultan Ismail early yesterday. Zakaria added that the department maintains strict guidelines on vehicle usage, stating, “The internal investigation will reveal if the driver followed the guidelines.” According to Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa, preliminary findings indicate that the 43-year-old driver was the sole occupant of the lorry at the time of the crash.

items.title: Port Klang dog death: Man and woman to be charged over alleged abuse of Rocky
items.summary: KLANG, Aug 20 — A man and a woman linked to the death of a dog named Rocky are scheduled to appear in court today. The case stems from an enforcement operation in Taman Teluk Gedong Indah, Port Klang, last month, during which Rocky died. Shah has denied abusing or killing Rocky during the operation on July 29.

items.title: PDRM raids Puchong diesel syndicate, makes RM919,022 seizure
items.summary: Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department (JKDNKA) Wildlife Crime Bureau/Special Intelligence Investigation (WCB/PSK) commander Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar said the raid, conducted under Ops Taring Bravo 1 from 3.30 am, was carried out in collaboration with the Selangor Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN). “Preliminary investigations found that the two individuals are believed to be the premise caretaker and lorry driver,” he said in a statement yesterday. Mohd Zaki said the premise was believed to have been operating as a storage and handling facility for subsidised diesel without a valid licence or permit.

items.title: Zayn Rayyan’s mother to learn appeal outcome on Sept 28 as court reserves decision
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 20 — The High Court here yesterday fixed Sept 28 for its decision on Ismanira Abdul Manaf’s appeal to overturn her conviction and five-year prison sentence for neglecting her six-year-old son, Zayn Rayyan Abdul Matin, resulting in physical injury three years ago. Judge Noor Hisham Ismail set the date after hearing submissions from both sides, including the prosecution’s cross-appeal against the sentence imposed on Ismanira, 31. Earlier, Lavanesh submitted that the court should allow the appeal and overturn his client’s conviction and sentence, arguing that the five-year prison term was excessive.

items.title: Kuala Kangsar police seek public help to identify woman found in suitcase in Sungai Perak
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 20 — Police are seeking the public’s assistance to identify the body of a woman found in a suitcase in Sungai Perak near Jeti Lembah in Kuala Kangsar on Friday after a fingerprint check found no matching record. Kuala Kangsar district police chief ACP Heisham Harun said efforts to identify the victim were also made through the Perak National Registration Department (JPN), but a search of her thumbprint also found no matching record. “When found, the woman was wearing a long-sleeved black-and-white striped shirt, black jeans and earrings.

items.title: Family of three killed in KL Immigration lorry crash buried in Kampar
items.summary: KAMPAR, Aug 20 — The remains of three family members who died in a crash involving a Malaysian Immigration Department (JIM) lorry at Jalan Sultan Ismail, Kuala Lumpur, yesterday were laid to rest at the Kampung Air Hitam Labu Muslim Cemetery here last night. Earlier, the remains of the retired soldier and his two daughters underwent a post-mortem at the National Institute of Forensic Medicine (IPFN), Kuala Lumpur Hospital, followed by funeral prayers at the Jamiul Ehsan Mosque in Jalan Pahang. Meanwhile, his wife, Norhayati Razali, 55, is currently receiving treatment at the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) of Kuala Lumpur Hospital.

items.title: DBKL to resurface 59km of KL roads in RM100m project
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 20 — A total of 59 kilometres (km) of protocol and main roads in the capital, covering about 1.3 million square metres, will be resurfaced in stages under the Eight-Road Resurfacing Programme. Also present was Kuala Lumpur Mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud. The first phase involves five main routes: Sultan Iskandar Highway-Jalan Damansara-Jalan Istana; Syed Putra Roundabout-Mid Valley Megamall (inbound and outbound); Jalan Sultan Ismail (Jalan Kuching slip road-Jalan Imbi); Jalan Ampang (Intermark slip road-Jalan Raja Chulan); and the highway entrance slip road facing the old airport (Kuala Lumpur-Seremban Highway Phase 1) up to the SPE Highway entrance slip road and the SPE Highway entrance slip road to the arch (Kuala Lumpur-Seremban Highway Phase 2).

items.title: Beyond the naked eye: What PM2.5, haze’s invisible threat, means for your health
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 20 — As Malaysians once again experience a resurgence in haze pollution and deteriorating air quality, many have begun taking precautions against its more visible health effects. While coughing, sore throats and irritated eyes may prompt people to take action, some of the more concerning pollutants associated with haze are invisible to the naked eye and may not always factor into how people protect themselves. Known as PM2.5, these microscopic fine particles — particulate matter (PM) measuring 2.5 micrometres or less in diameter — are small enough to penetrate deep into the lungs and potentially trigger adverse health effects beyond the respiratory system.

items.title: MACC urged to clarify status of two-month-old petroleum cargo commingling report
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Maritime industry observer Datuk Seri Jeyenderan Ramasamy has urged the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) to provide a written update on a report lodged in June concerning the alleged commingling or blending of petroleum cargo. He said the absence of an official response had created a serious operational situation, particularly as decisions involving the handling, movement and management of petroleum cargo could not responsibly be left in indefinite uncertainty. “Decisions affecting the handling, movement and management of petroleum cargo cannot responsibly be left in indefinite uncertainty.

items.title: Shahrir Samad says lawsuit not an act of revenge but to ensure enforcement powers are used properly
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Former Johor Bahru Member of Parliament Tan Sri Shahrir Abdul Samad told the High Court here today that his lawsuit was not intended as an act of revenge, but to ensure that enforcement powers are exercised appropriately. He said this when testifying in the lawsuit he filed against former Attorney General (AG) Tan Sri Tommy Thomas, former Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Chief Commissioner Latheefa Koya, the MACC, and the government regarding malicious prosecution. “Those powers must be exercised only after the fundamental aspects have been properly investigated,” said Shahrir, 76, in his witness statement.

items.title: Nga Kor Ming says Malaysia’s ethnic and cultural diversity must be preserved
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 19 — Malaysia’s ethnic and cultural diversity is a national strength that needs to be protected to maintain a harmonious, inclusive and progressive society, Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming says. He said the spirit of unity in diversity should remain a driving force for Malaysians, including staff of the Housing and Local Government Ministry (KPKT), to work together in developing the country. Speaking at the launch of Semarak Jiwa Merdeka @ KPKT to mark National Month here today, Nga said the independence Malaysians enjoy today had come at a cost, built on the unity, sacrifices and hard work of the nation’s people.

items.title: Indonesian Navy thwarts bid to smuggle 75.7 tonnes of tin sand worth RM17.27m to Malaysia
items.summary: JAKARTA, Aug 19 — The Indonesian Navy has thwarted a suspected attempt to smuggle about 75.7 tonnes of illegally mined tin sand to Malaysia from the Bangka Belitung Islands off the east coast of Sumatra, with the haul estimated at Rp76.04 billion (RM17.27 million). Indonesian Fleet Command chief Vice Admiral Denih Hendrata said the case came to light after naval personnel intercepted a truck carrying about eight tonnes of tin sand at a jetty in East Belitung on Aug 2, triggering a string of follow-up raids. The raids uncovered about 50 tonnes in Lenggang village on Aug 3, another 10 tonnes packed in 200 sacks the following day and another five tonnes on Aug 8, he said.

items.title: Malaysia’s defence spending driven by emerging threats, not just regional dynamics, says Khaled Nordin
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — The need for higher defence spending was driven not only by regional dynamics but also by emerging threats, said Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin. He said several developments had changed the government’s approach to defence policy and expenditure, including emerging challenges such as cyber and electromagnetic threats, as well as mass misinformation campaigns. This creates a more complex security environment for countries like Malaysia,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Former 1MDB CEO denies making deal with late lead prosecutor Sri Ram to testify in company’s favour
items.summary: Muhammad Shafee: Did Sri Ram interview you? Shahrol Azral: Yes. Shahrol Azral: Yes, once.

items.title: MOF: Unsubsidised petrol and diesel to rise 10-20 sen per litre from Aug 20-26
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Retail prices of unsubsidised petroleum products nationwide will increase by between 10 sen and 20 sen per litre for the August 20-26 period, driven by global geopolitical instability affecting crude oil prices and supplies. The price of unsubsidised RON95 will rise by 15 sen to RM3.77 per litre from RM3.62, while unsubsidised diesel will increase by 20 sen to RM4.67 per litre from RM4.47 previously. Prices of subsidised petroleum products remain unchanged, with BUDI Madani RON95 (BUDI95) at RM1.99 per litre and BUDI Madani Diesel (BUDI Diesel) at RM2.10 per litre.

items.title: Home minister orders Immigration to fully cooperate in fatal Maju Junction crash probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail has ordered the Malaysian Immigration Department to fully cooperate with authorities in the investigation into the early morning crash involving one of its lorries, which tragically claimed the lives of three family members. Expressing deep sorrow over the tragedy, Saifuddin Nasution also extended his condolences to the family members of the victims. “The entire Ministry of Home Affairs and Malaysian Immigration Department pray that the victims’ family will be given strength and resilience to face this difficult time.

items.title: No Malaysians reported affected by mudslides in northern Chile, says Malaysian rep in Santiago
items.summary: SANTIAGO (Chile), Aug 19 — No registered Malaysians have been reported involved or affected by mudslides following heavy rain in several areas in northern Chile since mid-August, according to the Embassy of Malaysia (Malawakil) in Santiago, Chile today. Malawakil Santiago said as of August 19, a total of 49 Malaysians have registered with the embassy, while it continues to monitor the weather situation in the affected areas. “Heavy rain hit several areas in northern Chile, particularly the Atacama and Antofagasta regions, triggering mudslides,” it said in a report on the extreme weather conditions and flash floods in northern Chile shared with Bernama.

items.title: Kota Bharu hospital says drug‑positive newborn now stable, no longer showing withdrawal symptoms
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 19 — A baby girl who tested positive for drugs after being born at Raja Perempuan Zainab II Hospital here is now in stable condition and no longer showing withdrawal symptoms. Kelantan Health director Dr Kasuadi Hussin said the baby, who remains under observation at the hospital’s Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU), was showing positive signs of recovery. On August 12, the baby girl tested positive for amphetamine and benzodiazepines after undergoing a urine test at the NICU of the hospital.

items.title: Chairman: MARA reviews MRSM outing guidelines amid probe into disappearance of two Form Four students in Alor Gajah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Majlis Amanah Rakyat (MARA) is reviewing the standard operating procedures (SOP) governing outings for students of its Mara Junior Science Colleges (MRSM) following the recent disappearance of two students. Its chairman Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the disappearance of the two Form Four students from MRSM Alor Gajah, Melaka, on August 11 was an isolated case and should not result in rules that could disrupt activities and programmes at MRSMs. The students, both 16, were reported missing on Aug 11 after receiving treatment at a health clinic and were found four days later near Pasar Seni in Kuala Lumpur.

items.title: CM: Penang seeks federal backing for proposed international financial centre in Budget 2027
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 19 — Penang is hoping for its proposed international financial centre (PIFC) to be approved under Budget 2027. Chief minister Chow Kon Yeow said the state hopes to pitch the proposed PIFC to the Finance Ministry with the white paper prepared by an appointed consultant. He said the PIFC could eventually be known as the Penang Technology Financial Centre, to better reflect its intended purpose of financing technology development in the state.
